page: Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores clocked at 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for INT8 and BF16 workloads, alongside hardware cryptographic extensions.

Memory capacity is configured with 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a compute-centric 2:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 15 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. It features zero local instance storage and zero GPUs, requiring remote EBS volumes for non-volatile storage and operating solely on CPU execution paths.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong raw processor performance, placing in the top quartile across Geekbench single-core, multi-core, and PassMark CPU metrics. Compute-dense tasks like cryptographic encryption, physics simulation, and compressed data decompression also register in the top 25 percent. Instruction-level optimizations yield high throughput for small-parameter machine learning inference, while memory-heavy database operations and uncached memory bandwidth fall in the middle 50 percent.

The 2.0 GB per core configuration provides a cost-efficient resource density for CPU-heavy deployments that do not justify the overhead of broader memory allocations. Workloads best aligned with the c8i.8xlarge include compute-bound data processing pipelines, web serving clusters, continuous integration builds, and small-model CPU inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro virtual machine featuring a 32-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz and 64.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory. Operating on an x86_64 architecture with 16 physical cores, it features 480 MB of L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, routing all disk traffic over a 15 Gbps network interface. Benchmark evaluations show upper-quartile ratings for single-core and multi-core integer performance, data compression, encryption routines, and static web serving, with average throughput on uncached memory access and database transactions. Its 2 GB per vCPU ratio represents a hardware profile suited for high-density compute tasks, batch processing, and CPU-driven inference.
